fonts.title: Times New Roman
fonts.note: Georgia not installed locally. No font files distributed.

screens.title: Welcome
screens.purpose: Players choose whether to log in or create an account. This preserves the original simple welcome screen and provides the entry point for personalized progress.
screens.rule: LOG IN → 06; SIGN UP → 02.

screens.title: Sign up
screens.purpose: Players supply an account name and password. A successful signup takes them to login rather than entering the game automatically.
screens.rule: SIGN UP → 05 (sample success); BACK → 01. Validation variants: 03 and 04.

screens.title: Signup · missing fields
screens.purpose: An inline message explains that the required fields are missing. The form stays available so the player can correct the problem without losing context.
screens.rule: Keep the same form; do not create an account until valid. Preview SIGN UP follows the corrected path.

screens.title: Signup · duplicate name
screens.purpose: An inline message explains that the account name already exists. Players can choose another name or return to login.
screens.rule: Keep credentials masked; do not reveal another account’s details.

screens.title: Signup success → login
screens.purpose: A success message confirms account creation on the login form. The player then logs in to reach the main menu.
screens.rule: LOG IN → 08 (new-player example). Real code must read actual account progress.

screens.title: Log in
screens.purpose: Players enter their account name and password to access their saved progress. The preview is a visual route demonstration and does not authenticate or collect credentials.
screens.rule: LOG IN → 08 (sample success); BACK → 01; error variant → 07.

screens.title: Login · invalid credentials
screens.purpose: A neutral error message says the name or password is invalid. Players can correct their entries and retry without disclosing which credential was wrong.
screens.rule: Stay on login; LOG IN previews a successful corrected attempt.

screens.title: Main menu · no progress
screens.purpose: New players can start a game, open load/settings, or quit. Continue is disabled and explained because no resumable checkpoint exists.
screens.rule: NEW GAME → 11; LOAD → 30; SETTINGS → 32; LOG OUT → 34; QUIT → 35. Account name and Logout are additions.

screens.title: Main menu · returning player
screens.purpose: Returning players can continue their latest checkpoint or start a new game. This gives Continue a clear purpose and protects existing progress before a restart.
screens.rule: CONTINUE → 13 (sample checkpoint); NEW GAME → 10.

screens.title: New game confirmation
screens.purpose: A returning player confirms starting a new playthrough. The message distinguishes restarting current progress from deleting manual saves.
screens.rule: START NEW → 11; CANCEL → 09. Keep manual saves unless the player explicitly deletes them.

screens.title: How to play
screens.purpose: Players learn the story controls before playing. The explanation clearly distinguishes narrative choices from scored Reading Checks.
screens.rule: NEXT → 12; BACK → 08. Space advances narrative only, never submits an assessment answer.

screens.title: Introduction
screens.purpose: The introduction establishes the player’s role before Chapter 1 begins. It preserves the existing brief servant premise, with final story copy still to be supplied by the team.
screens.rule: PLAY → 13; BACK → 11. Text is source placeholder, not an approved final script.

screens.title: Story · dialogue
screens.purpose: The player reads a character’s dialogue in the existing burgundy-and-gold panel. NEXT advances the conversation, while MENU opens navigation without advancing the story.
screens.rule: NEXT / Space → 14; MENU / Esc → 26. Restore the exact scene when returning from a menu.

screens.title: Story · thoughts
screens.purpose: The lighter panel and italic text distinguish the player’s private thoughts from spoken dialogue. Players advance when they finish reading.
screens.rule: NEXT / Space → 15; MENU / Esc → 26.

screens.title: Story · narrative choice
screens.purpose: The player chooses how to respond to the character. These choices affect story branches and relationships, not comprehension score or difficulty.
screens.rule: All three preview choices → 16; real game must restore the chosen branch. Story choice text is illustrative.

screens.title: Story · branch continuation
screens.purpose: The story acknowledges the chosen narrative action before the Reading Check. This prevents a story choice from jumping directly to a fabricated comprehension result.
screens.rule: NEXT → 17. Branch-specific dialogue is sample content; author each actual branch separately.

screens.title: Reading Check · unanswered
screens.purpose: A separate passage and question measure comprehension. Submit stays disabled until an answer is selected, and the player can read at their own pace.
screens.rule: B → 18; A or C → 19. MENU pauses; no time limit or autoplay submission.

screens.title: Reading Check · selected B
screens.purpose: The selected answer is visibly highlighted before submission. Players can change their selection until Submit records their first attempt.
screens.rule: SUBMIT → 20; A/C → 19. Selection alone must not score or advance the question.

screens.title: Reading Check · selected A
screens.purpose: This variant shows a selected incorrect answer before submission. It demonstrates the wrong-answer route without disclosing correctness before the player submits.
screens.rule: SUBMIT → 21; B → 18. The example groups A/C into the incorrect selection route.

screens.title: Reading Check · correct feedback
screens.purpose: The player sees confirmation and a passage-based explanation. The first submitted answer is locked, and the next action advances to another question.
screens.rule: NEXT QUESTION → 22 (representative final-question jump); the actual game must show questions 2–4.

screens.title: Reading Check · incorrect feedback
screens.purpose: The player receives a supportive explanation of the correct reasoning. The incorrect first attempt remains recorded; feedback does not offer a score-changing retry.
screens.rule: NEXT QUESTION → 22 (representative final-question jump). No resubmission for this scored question.

screens.title: Reading Check · final question
screens.purpose: The final-question state marks the end of a five-question check. It reuses the same question layout so the team can implement one reusable assessment view.
screens.rule: SUBMIT → 22b after first-attempt recording. This is a fixed selected-state preview; sample passage repeats for layout only.

screens.title: Reading Check · final feedback
screens.purpose: The final submitted answer receives the same explanatory feedback as earlier questions. View Results then moves to difficulty analysis rather than presenting another question.
screens.rule: VIEW RESULTS → 23. Reuse the feedback component with a final-question action variant; incorrect final feedback follows the same route.

screens.title: Preparing the next challenge
screens.purpose: A brief status panel tells the player that the completed answers are being analyzed. Progress is recorded before optional model analysis so a timeout does not lose the completed check.
screens.rule: NEXT (preview success) → 24; MODEL UNAVAILABLE (preview test route) → 25. Real Java code should transition automatically with a bounded timeout.

screens.title: Chapter results · normal
screens.purpose: The result combines a comprehension score, first-answer count, and the next difficulty. Java validates any model recommendation before the player continues.
screens.rule: CONTINUE → 40. 80% / Medium is illustrative, not a fixed rule or a model guarantee.

screens.title: Chapter results · model fallback
screens.purpose: The result remains usable when the optional model fails or times out. Java applies its deterministic fallback policy and explains the outcome without alarming the player.
screens.rule: CONTINUE → 40. Easy is an example outcome; use actual validated policy output.

screens.title: Game menu / pause
screens.purpose: This menu pauses narrative progression and exposes save, load, settings, and exit actions. Return restores the exact prior scene or assessment state instead of restarting it.
screens.rule: SAVE → 27; LOAD → 30; SETTINGS → 32; MAIN MENU → 33; RETURN → captured previous scene in the preview.

screens.title: Save · occupied and empty slots
screens.purpose: Players can identify saves by chapter, scene, difficulty, and timestamp. Empty slots accept new saves, while occupied slots require overwrite confirmation.
screens.rule: Slot 1 → 29; empty Slot 2–6 → 28. Preserve the original six-slot page visually; finalize count with backend team.

screens.title: Save · success
screens.purpose: A visible confirmation appears only after persistence succeeds. The player stays on Save and can return to the held scene without losing their place.
screens.rule: RETURN → previous screen. Example shows a newly populated Slot 2; overwrite instead updates the chosen occupied slot.

screens.title: Save · overwrite confirmation
screens.purpose: The player confirms replacing an occupied slot before data is changed. Cancel preserves the existing save and returns to the slot list.
screens.rule: OVERWRITE → 28 after successful write; CANCEL → 27. Failure route is 39.

screens.title: Load · occupied and empty slots
screens.purpose: Players select a saved checkpoint using meaningful metadata. Empty slots are disabled, so the interface does not pretend to load nonexistent progress.
screens.rule: Slot 1 → 31 if current state is unsaved, otherwise resume immediately. If called from main menu with no active game, skip discard confirmation.

screens.title: Load · unsaved progress warning
screens.purpose: The player confirms discarding unsaved session progress before loading a checkpoint. Cancel returns to Load without changing the current session.
screens.rule: LOAD SAVE → 13 only after validation and successful restore; CANCEL → 30. Invalid save route is 38.

screens.title: Settings
screens.purpose: The existing audio and reading-speed controls retain their two-column layout. Text-size controls are a proposed accessibility addition, and autoplay pauses whenever a Reading Check is active.
screens.rule: RETURN restores caller. Preview sliders/text-size are appearance specifications, not working controls.

screens.title: Return to main menu confirmation
screens.purpose: The player confirms leaving an active session before unsaved changes are discarded. This distinguishes Main Menu from Return, which resumes the held game.
screens.rule: MAIN MENU → 09; CANCEL → previous screen. Saved checkpoints remain available.

screens.title: Logout confirmation
screens.purpose: The player confirms ending their authenticated session. Logout clears session access, but keeps saved progress associated with the account.
screens.rule: LOG OUT → 01; CANCEL → 09. If active unsaved play exists, use the same loss warning and allow cancel.

screens.title: Quit confirmation
screens.purpose: The existing quit card warns that unsaved progress will be lost. Players can cancel without navigating or changing game state.
screens.rule: QUIT → 36 (terminal-state representation); CANCEL restores caller. Real app closes its window only on confirmation.

screens.title: Application closed · flow endpoint
screens.purpose: This reference-only endpoint represents the application window closing. It is not a new screen for the JavaFX team to implement.
screens.rule: Preview RESTART → 01; real program has no rendered screen after exit.

screens.title: Story complete
screens.purpose: The player receives a clear endpoint after the last available chapter is completed. They can return to the main menu without a Continue button pointing to nonexistent content.
screens.rule: MAIN MENU → 09 with story-complete metadata. Continue should replay or be disabled only if the team explicitly specifies that behavior.

screens.title: Load · unreadable save
screens.purpose: An error explains that the selected checkpoint could not be loaded. The current session and save data are preserved so the player can choose another slot.
screens.rule: BACK TO LOAD → 30. Do not partially restore or silently delete a damaged save.

screens.title: Save · persistence failed
screens.purpose: The player is told that the save did not succeed and the session remains unsaved. Retry attempts persistence again; cancel restores the session without claiming progress was saved.
screens.rule: RETRY → 28 is the successful retry example; CANCEL → previous screen. Keep the old slot intact on failure.

screens.title: Next chapter · loading / completion
screens.purpose: The player sees a transition while the next chapter and validated difficulty are loaded. If there is no next chapter, the game shows Story Complete instead of entering an empty scene.
screens.rule: NEXT CHAPTER → 13 is a reusable-layout sample; STORY FINISHED → 37 is a reviewer test route. Real application chooses automatically.
